ideas.title: Add Canvas State Snapshot Persistence
ideas.description: Create a useCanvasSnapshots hook that extends the existing HistoryContext to support named snapshots with persistence across sessions. Users can save, name, and restore specific canvas states. Builds on the usePromptHistory pattern for CRUD operations with favorites and search.
ideas.rationale: The usePromptHistory hook (src/hooks/usePromptHistory.ts) already establishes the pattern: PromptRecord interface, StorageManager backing, favorites, timestamps, search. The HistoryContext exists for in-session undo/redo but lacks persistence. Combining these patterns enables a complete design versioning system.
existing_patterns: usePromptHistory: PromptRecord with id, isFavorite, useCount, timestamps
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add canvasSnapshotsStorage instance to storageManager.ts. 2. Create SnapshotRecord interface following PromptRecord: id, name, thumbnail, canvasState (JSON), isFavorite, createdAt. 3. Create useCanvasSnapshots hook with addSnapshot, restoreSnapshot, renameSnapshot, deleteSnapshot, toggleFavorite, searchSnapshots. 4. Integrate with CanvasEditor for save/restore buttons.

ideas.title: Extend Canvas Commands with Batch Element Operations
ideas.description: Add BatchDeleteElements, BatchUpdateElements, and BatchMoveElements commands following the established batch command pattern from imageCommands.ts. Enables bulk operations on multiple canvas elements via voice or UI.
ideas.rationale: BatchUpscaleCommand and BatchRemoveBackgroundCommand in imageCommands.ts demonstrate the batch pattern: iterate over items, collect results/errors, handle partial failures gracefully. Canvas commands only have single-element operations. The Command interface and ToolSchemas registry support this extension.
existing_patterns: BatchUpscaleCommand: for-loop with try-catch per item, results[] and errors[] collection
DeleteElementCommand.execute: single element deletion with context.canvasCallbacks
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add BatchDeleteElementsSchema, BatchUpdateElementsSchema to validationSchemas.ts: z.object({ element_ids: z.array(z.string()) }). 2. Create BatchDeleteElementsCommand following BatchUpscaleCommand structure. 3. Create BatchUpdateElementsCommand for bulk property changes. 4. Register in ToolSchemas and ensure actionExecutor routes correctly.

ideas.title: Add Error Recovery Suggestions Hook
ideas.description: Create a useErrorRecovery hook that provides actionable recovery suggestions based on the existing error classification system. Maps error types (network, cors, timeout, api, etc.) to specific user actions (retry, check API key, wait for rate limit).
ideas.rationale: The errorHandler.ts already classifies errors into structured NetworkError types with retryable flags and dispatches 'error-tracked' CustomEvents. The withRetry function handles automatic retries. This infrastructure enables a user-facing recovery suggestion system without new error handling logic.
existing_patterns: classifyError: returns { type: 'network'|'cors'|'timeout'|'api', retryable: boolean, message: string }
useErrorMetrics: listens to events, aggregates metrics
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create RECOVERY_SUGGESTIONS map: { network: 'Check internet connection', api: 'Verify API key in Settings', timeout: 'Try again - server was slow', cors: 'This operation not supported' }. 2. Create useErrorRecovery hook listening to 'error-tracked' events. 3. Return { lastError, suggestions, canRetry, retryAction }. 4. Integrate with Toast for actionable error messages.

ideas.title: Add Layout Expert Agent to Registry
ideas.description: Add a 'Layout Expert' specialized agent to AGENT_REGISTRY for banner composition, element positioning, safe zones, and visual hierarchy. Uses the existing AgentDefinition interface with appropriate keywords for automatic routing.
ideas.rationale: The agentRegistry.ts has 4 well-established agents (Benno, Art Director, Copy Specialist, Tech Wizard) following AgentDefinition interface. The getAgentSuggestions function handles new agents automatically via keyword matching - no routing changes needed. Layout/positioning expertise is missing from current agents.
existing_patterns: AgentDefinition: { id, name, description, capabilities, systemPrompt, keywords, icon }
Art Director agent structure: keywords array, capabilities array
Keyword scoring in getAgentSuggestions: score += 0.3 per keyword match
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add new AgentDefinition object to AGENT_REGISTRY. 2. Set id: 'layout-expert', name: 'Layout Expert'. 3. Keywords: ['layout', 'position', 'center', 'align', 'space', 'safe zone', 'composition', 'hierarchy', 'arrange', 'grid']. 4. Capabilities: ['list_elements', 'update_element', 'analyze_banner']. 5. SystemPrompt focused on LinkedIn safe zones, visual hierarchy, element spacing.

ideas.title: Add Model Performance Comparison Utility
ideas.description: Create a compareModelPerformance utility that combines MODEL_METADATA_REGISTRY theoretical scores with useModelMetrics actual usage data to rank and recommend models. Enables data-driven model selection that improves with usage.
ideas.rationale: MODEL_METADATA_REGISTRY (modelRouter.ts) has qualityScore, avgResponseTime, costPerCall for each model. useModelMetrics aggregates actual stats.byModel with calls, avgTime, successRate. These exist independently - combining them enables intelligent recommendations based on real performance.
existing_patterns: stats.byModel[modelId]: { calls, avgTime, successRate, errors, totalCost }
getModelMetadataById: memoized lookup for model metadata
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add getModelRecommendations(operation: OperationType) to modelRouter.ts. 2. Fetch theoretical scores from REGISTRY and actual stats from modelMetricsStorage. 3. Compute weighted score: 40% actual successRate (if data exists), 30% response time, 20% qualityScore, 10% cost efficiency. 4. Return sorted array of { modelId, score, hasUsageData }. 5. Optionally show 'Recommended' badge in ModelSelector based on this ranking.

ideas.title: Add Password Visibility Toggle to AuthModal
ideas.description: Add a show/hide password toggle button to the password input field in the authentication modal, allowing users to verify their password entry before submission.
ideas.rationale: Password visibility toggles are a standard UX pattern that reduce login friction and prevent errors. Currently users must type passwords blindly, which can lead to typos and failed login attempts especially on mobile devices.
ideas.current_state: The password input field uses type='password' (line 348) without any visibility toggle. Users cannot see what they've typed, making it difficult to verify input accuracy. The input has icons for validation states but no visibility toggle.
ideas.proposed_change: Add showPassword state boolean. Create an eye/eye-off icon button inside the password input field (similar to the username validation indicator pattern at lines 295-311). Toggle between type='password' and type='text' on click. Use Material Icons 'visibility' and 'visibility_off' icons. Position at right-4 with -translate-y-1/2 styling like existing icons.
ideas.user_benefit: Users can verify their password entry before submission, reducing failed login attempts and frustration, especially on mobile where typing is more error-prone.

ideas.title: Add Visible Previous Button to OnboardingTour
ideas.description: Add a visible 'Previous' button to the onboarding tour component allowing users to navigate backwards through tour steps without relying on keyboard shortcuts.
ideas.rationale: While ArrowLeft keyboard navigation exists, there's no visible Previous button. Users may miss information or want to review previous steps. Most users won't discover keyboard shortcuts without visible affordance.
ideas.current_state: The tour has Next/Finish and Skip buttons (lines 209-211, 268-286). ArrowLeft keyboard shortcut works (lines 113-115) but there's no visible Previous button. Users can only go forward visually or skip entirely.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a Previous button next to Skip when currentStep > 0. Use text-xs font-bold text-zinc-500 hover:text-white uppercase tracking-wider styling like the Skip button. Add Material Icon 'arrow_back' before the text. On click: setCurrentStep(c => c - 1). Place it in the button group at lines 208-214 (spotlight mode) and 268-275 (centered mode).
ideas.user_benefit: Users can easily review previous tour steps without needing to restart the entire tour or know keyboard shortcuts, making onboarding more user-friendly.

ideas.title: Add Voice Status Text Label During Connection States
ideas.description: Add a brief animated text badge below the voice button to clarify connection states (Connecting, Connected, Failed) without requiring tooltip hover.
ideas.rationale: The voice button uses color and icon changes to indicate state but users may not understand what amber spinning sync vs red error_outline means without hovering. Explicit text feedback reduces confusion.
ideas.current_state: Voice button (lines 170-217) shows different states via gradient backgrounds and icons but state meaning is only conveyed via title/aria-label tooltips. Users must hover to understand 'Connecting to Benno...' vs 'Connection failed - Click to retry'.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a small text badge below the voice button during transitional states. Wrap the button in a relative container with flex-col. Add a span with absolute positioning showing: 'Connecting...' (text-amber-400), 'Connected' (text-green-400, fade out after 2s), 'Failed' (text-red-400). Use text-[8px] font-bold uppercase tracking-wider. Add aria-live='polite' for screen reader announcements.
ideas.user_benefit: Users immediately understand voice agent status without hovering for tooltips, improving trust and reducing confusion about the voice feature state.

ideas.title: Add Focus Ring to Form Inputs for Accessibility
ideas.description: Enhance the visibility of focus states on form inputs by adding visible focus rings in addition to subtle border color changes.
ideas.rationale: Current inputs use border color changes on focus (border-purple-500/50) which may not provide sufficient contrast for users with low vision. WCAG 2.1 requires focus indicators to be clearly visible (at least 3:1 contrast).
ideas.current_state: AuthModal inputs use 'focus:border-purple-500/50' (line 258, 272, 293, etc). GenerativeSidebar textarea uses 'focus:border-pink-500' (line 386). INPUT_NEU in styles.ts adds glow but no ring. These are subtle color changes that may fail accessibility requirements.
ideas.proposed_change: Add 'focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-500/50 focus:ring-offset-2 focus:ring-offset-zinc-900' to all text inputs in AuthModal and GenerativeSidebar. Update INPUT_NEU in styles.ts to include ring styles. Add 'contrast-more:focus:ring-4 contrast-more:focus:ring-white' for high-contrast mode support (matching Toast.tsx pattern lines 127-128).
ideas.user_benefit: Users navigating with keyboard can clearly see which element is focused, improving accessibility for users with visual impairments and those who prefer keyboard navigation.

ideas.title: Add Character Count to Prompt Textarea with Length Guidance
ideas.description: Add a live character count indicator to the prompt textarea in GenerativeSidebar with color feedback to guide users toward optimal prompt lengths.
ideas.rationale: AI image generation prompts have optimal length ranges. Too short may lack detail, too long may confuse the model. Users currently have no feedback about prompt length or guidance on ideal ranges for best results.
ideas.current_state: The textarea for background generation (line 385-390) has placeholder text but no character count or length guidance. Users type without knowing if their prompt is too brief or approaching model limits. The placeholder suggests a prompt style but doesn't indicate length.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a character count display below the textarea: '{genPrompt.length} / 500'. Apply color coding: text-zinc-500 for 0-50 (add hint 'Add more detail'), text-zinc-400 for 50-100, text-green-500 for 100-350 (optimal range), text-yellow-500 for 350-450 (verbose), text-red-400 for 450+ (may truncate). Add aria-describedby linking to helper text explaining optimal 100-300 char range.
ideas.user_benefit: Users receive real-time feedback on prompt length, helping them craft more effective prompts that produce better AI generation results. Reduces wasted generation attempts from under-specified prompts.

ideas.title: Proxy Voice WebSocket Connections Through Server to Protect API Keys
ideas.description: The OpenAI Realtime API key is retrieved via `/api/user/voice-key` endpoint and sent to the client. The client uses this key directly in WebSocket subprotocol headers (`openai-insecure-api-key.${this.apiKey}`) in `openaiRealtimeClient.ts` line 337-341. This exposes the actual API key in browser developer tools, network inspection, and client-side JavaScript memory.
ideas.rationale: Exposing API keys to the client-side is a critical security flaw. The key can be stolen via browser extensions, XSS attacks, man-in-the-middle proxies, or simply by users inspecting network traffic. A compromised OpenAI key could result in significant financial costs (voice API pricing) and abuse. The key is literally named 'insecure-api-key' in the WebSocket protocol.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
ideas.currentRisk: OpenAI API keys are fully exposed to client browsers, enabling unauthorized API usage, potential financial abuse, and key theft
ideas.remediation: Implement a server-side WebSocket proxy that maintains the OpenAI Realtime connection on the backend. Architecture: Client ↔ Your Server (WebSocket) ↔ OpenAI (WebSocket with API key). The client connects to your server which relays audio bidirectionally. This keeps the API key entirely server-side. Consider using a Node.js WebSocket library (ws) to proxy connections.

ideas.title: Implement Server-Side Password Strength Validation
ideas.description: The signup endpoint in `server/src/routes/auth.ts` (line 17-21) only validates that password is a non-empty string (`!password || typeof password !== 'string'`). There are no password complexity requirements enforced, allowing users to register with trivially weak passwords like '1', 'a', or 'password'.
ideas.rationale: Weak passwords are a primary attack vector even with rate limiting and account lockout in place. Users often reuse passwords across services, and weak passwords can be compromised through offline dictionary attacks if the database is ever breached. The existing Argon2 hashing protects against rainbow tables but not against dictionary attacks on weak passwords.
ideas.currentRisk: Users can set trivially weak passwords (e.g., '1', 'password123'), making accounts vulnerable to credential stuffing even with account lockout protection
ideas.remediation: Add server-side password validation middleware requiring: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number. Consider checking against Have I Been Pwned API for breached passwords. Example validation: `if (password.length < 8 || !/[A-Z]/.test(password) || !/[a-z]/.test(password) || !/[0-9]/.test(password)) return error;`

ideas.title: Add Input Length Limits and Sanitization for AI Prompts
ideas.description: AI endpoints in `server/src/routes/ai.ts` accept user prompts without enforcing maximum length limits or sanitization. The `/api/ai/chat`, `/api/ai/image/generate`, and `/api/ai/image/edit` routes pass prompts directly to external APIs. Only `/api/ai/prompt/enhance` has basic string validation (`typeof prompt !== 'string'`).
ideas.rationale: Without input validation, malicious users could: 1) Submit extremely long prompts (megabytes) causing excessive API costs and timeouts, 2) Attempt prompt injection attacks to manipulate AI behavior or extract system prompts, 3) Abuse the service for generating harmful content via carefully crafted prompts.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption / CWE-74: Prompt Injection
ideas.currentRisk: Resource exhaustion from oversized prompts, potential prompt injection attacks, excessive API costs from abuse
ideas.remediation: 1. Add maximum length validation for all prompts (e.g., 10,000 characters). 2. Implement a prompt validation middleware that runs before AI routes. 3. Log and monitor for suspicious patterns like 'ignore previous instructions', 'you are now', or system prompt extraction attempts. 4. Consider implementing semantic content filtering for generated outputs.

ideas.title: Enable Content Safety Filters on Generate-Layer Endpoint
ideas.description: In `server/src/routes/replicate.ts` line 342, the generate-layer endpoint has `disable_safety_checker: true` hard-coded, explicitly bypassing Replicate's content moderation. This is the only endpoint where safety is explicitly disabled - other endpoints have it enabled or use defaults.
ideas.rationale: Disabling content safety filters specifically for the generate-layer endpoint creates an attack vector for generating inappropriate content. While other endpoints have safety enabled, users could target this specific endpoint to bypass moderation. This could expose the platform to legal liability and Replicate ToS violations.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-1188: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource
ideas.currentRisk: The generate-layer endpoint bypasses content moderation, enabling generation of potentially harmful or policy-violating images
ideas.remediation: Remove `disable_safety_checker: true` from line 342 in replicate.ts. The default Replicate behavior with safety enabled should be sufficient for professional use cases. If there's a legitimate need for unfiltered generation, make it a server-controlled configuration with audit logging, not hard-coded.

ideas.title: Add Explicit .env.local to .gitignore
ideas.description: The `.gitignore` contains `*.local` pattern and explicit `.env` and `.env.test` entries. While `*.local` should match `.env.local`, some git versions handle dotfile glob patterns inconsistently. Multiple .env files exist: `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.test`, `server/.env`, and `.auto-claude/.env`.
ideas.rationale: Environment files containing API keys (OPENAI, REPLICATE, OPENROUTER, etc.) must never be committed. Even brief accidental commits persist in git history. The current setup relies on glob patterns which may behave differently across git versions and platforms.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
ideas.currentRisk: Potential accidental commit of environment files if gitignore patterns don't match on all systems
ideas.remediation: Explicitly add all environment files to .gitignore: `.env.local`, `server/.env`, `.auto-claude/.env`. Run `git status` to verify. Consider adding a pre-commit hook using `git-secrets` or `detect-secrets` to scan for API key patterns before each commit.
